name: ktkit
description: A spec-driven development toolkit for Claude Code: twenty skills covering the path from a problem somebody described in chat to a reviewed spec, an executed change, and a durable record of both. raise-issue frames that problem first -- it labels every fact with where it came from and how far it can be trusted, refuses to name a cause, and blocks until you confirm it understood the right problem. chain is the entry point for all four of its lanes -- BUG, CR, NR and TRIVIAL -- and runs the path as one closed loop: it resolves the open questions each phase raises by dispatching resolver subagents, records every answer in an append-only ledger the later phases read instead of re-deriving, and stops only for what could not be settled and would be expensive to get wrong. docs-review audits a document set with a team of agents that run concurrently and challenge each other's findings. spec-recon adds the axis a document reviewer cannot reach — it measures source code, binary artifacts and version-control state, and gates every claim that something is missing behind an agent that tries to refute it. analyze-feat, rca, cr-delta, feat-req-specs and bug-fix-specs turn a request into a reviewed specification -- cr-delta answers the question a change request asks and a feature request does not, which finished work this undoes, and answers it from the run's task ledger rather than by re-reading the repository; feat-req-execute and bug-fix-execute carry it out; ccompact and ccontinue keep a long pipeline alive across compaction; escalation-ladder resolves unknowns from the repository before asking you; confirm-with-me gates a single irreversible step; pr-writeup rewrites an existing pull request's title and description from the bodies of its own commits and the changed-file stat, never from the diff, and refuses every forge write but that one; create-pr opens a pull request from a branch into dev, develop or a named target and writes its title and body from the full bodies of the commits it carries, the issue it is for and what the session already established, never from the diff, then hands it to resolve-conflict-pr; resolve-conflict-pr merges a conflicted pull request's base into its head in a detached worktree of its own, never the branch you have checked out, explains each hunk from the commits on both sides, proves with a script that no line either side added was lost, and pushes the merge back without ever rebasing or force-pushing; translate-file translates a file without touching its identifiers; help prints an index of all of them, and a page per skill that is checked against that skill's own argument surface rather than written once and left to rot. Every skill writes to one fixed artifact root, runs a preflight that proves a capability with a real request instead of trusting a tool's own error message, and refuses to start when spec-kit or superpowers is missing rather than quietly doing something else.
